svg.title: How spatial windows and key order work
svg.desc: Apply the same pad/partition transform to Q, K and V · one token is one spatial position within one head
svg.text: How spatial windows and key order work
Apply the same pad/partition transform to Q, K and V · one token is one spatial position within one head
Q, K and V remain separate
Shift phases: (s_x, s_y) = (0,0), (4,4), (4,0), (0,4). Extra zeros fill the bottom / right tail.
Pixels stay in place; padding adds empty cells.
Query q54 retrieves values from all 64 keys.
Memory order · Q stays natural; K and V share the same permutation π
Same index array for both operands
which value belongs to each key.
After attention, reshape windows into the padded field and crop [s_y:s_y+H, s_x:s_x+W].
Shifts use zero padding and cropping; they do not cyclically roll pixels to the opposite image edge.
Logical tensor flow · shapes omit batch unless shown · operations may be fused in CUDA
